3: //! Signal driver
4: 
5: use crate::io::driver::{Driver as IoDriver, Interest};

12: use std::ptr;
13: use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};
14: use std::task::{Context, Poll, RawWaker, RawWakerVTable, Waker};
15: use std::time::Duration;

17: /// Responsible for registering wakeups when an OS signal is received, and
18: /// subsequently dispatching notifications to any signal listeners as appropriate.
19: ///
20: /// Note: this driver relies on having an enabled IO driver in order to listen to
21: /// pipe write wakeups.
22: #[derive(Debug)]
23: pub(crate) struct Driver {
24:     /// Thread parker. The `Driver` park implementation delegates to this.
25:     park: IoDriver,
26: 
27:     /// A pipe for receiving wake events from the signal handler
28:     receiver: PollEvented<UnixStream>,
29: 
30:     /// Shared state
31:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
32:     signal_policy: SignalPolicy,
33:     registry_plan: RegistryPlan,
34:     pipe_plan: PipePlan,
35:     park_plan: ParkPlan,
36:     reap_plan: ReapPlan,
37: }
38: 
39: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
40: pub(crate) struct Handle {
41:     inner: Weak<Inner>,
42: }
43: 
44: #[derive(Debug)]
45: pub(super) struct Inner(());
46: 
47: // ===== impl Driver =====
48: 
49: impl Driver {
50:     /// Creates a new signal `Driver` instance that delegates wakeups to `park`.
51:     pub(crate) fn new(park: IoDriver) -> io::Result<Self> {
52:         use std::mem::ManuallyDrop;
53:         use std::os::unix::io::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd};
54: 
55:         // NB: We give each driver a "fresh" receiver file descriptor to avoid
56:         // the issues described in alexcrichton/tokio-process#42.
57:         //
58:         // In the past we would reuse the actual receiver file descriptor and
59:         // swallow any errors around double registration of the same descriptor.
60:         // I'm not sure if the second (failed) registration simply doesn't end
61:         // up receiving wake up notifications, or there could be some race
62:         // condition when consuming readiness events, but having distinct
63:         // descriptors for distinct PollEvented instances appears to mitigate
64:         // this.
65:         //
66:         // Unfortunately we cannot just use a single global PollEvented instance
67:         // either, since we can't compare Handles or assume they will always
68:         // point to the exact same reactor.
69:         //
70:         // Mio 0.7 removed `try_clone()` as an API due to unexpected behavior
71:         // with registering dups with the same reactor. In this case, duping is
72:         // safe as each dup is registered with separate reactors **and** we
73:         // only expect at least one dup to receive the notification.
74: 
75:         // Manually drop as we don't actually own this instance of UnixStream.
76:         let receiver_fd = globals().receiver.as_raw_fd();
77: 
78:         // safety: there is nothing unsafe about this, but the `from_raw_fd` fn is marked as unsafe.
79:         let original =
80:             ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::from_raw_fd(receiver_fd) });
81:         let receiver = UnixStream::from_std(original.try_clone()?);
82:         let receiver = PollEvented::new_with_interest_and_handle(
83:             receiver,
84:             Interest::READABLE | Interest::WRITABLE,
85:             park.handle(),
86:         )?;
87: 
88:         Ok(Self {
89:             park,
90:             receiver,
91:             inner: Arc::new(Inner(())),
92:             signal_policy: SignalPolicy::standard(),
93:             registry_plan: RegistryPlan::standard(),
94:             pipe_plan: PipePlan::standard(),
95:             park_plan: ParkPlan::standard(),
96:             reap_plan: ReapPlan::standard(),
97:         }
98:         .with_initialized_policies())
99:     }
100: 
101:     /// Returns a handle to this event loop which can be sent across threads
102:     /// and can be used as a proxy to the event loop itself.
103:     pub(crate) fn handle(&self) -> Handle {
104:         Handle {
105:             inner: Arc::downgrade(&self.inner),
106:         }
107:     }
108: 
109:     fn process(&self) {
110:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
111:         //
112:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
113:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
114:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
115:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
116: 
117:         let ev = match self.receiver.registration().poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
118:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
119:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
120:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
121:         };
122: 
123:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
124:         // if another signal has come in.
125:         let mut buf = [0; 128];
126:         let view_len = self.pipe_drain_view_len(buf.len());
127:         loop {
128:             match (&*self.receiver).read(&mut buf[..view_len]) {
129:                 Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
130:                 Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
131:                 Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
132:                 Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
133:             }
134:         }
135: 
136:         self.receiver.registration().clear_readiness(ev);
137: 
138:         // Broadcast any signals which were received
139:         if self.should_broadcast_recorded_events() {
140:             globals().broadcast();
141:         }
142:     }
143: }
144: 
145: const NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE: RawWakerVTable = RawWakerVTable::new(noop_clone, noop, noop, noop);
146: 
147: unsafe fn noop_clone(_data: *const ()) -> RawWaker {
148:     RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)
149: }
150: 
151: unsafe fn noop(_data: *const ()) {}
152: 
153: // ===== impl Park for Driver =====
154: 
155: impl Park for Driver {
156:     type Unpark = <IoDriver as Park>::Unpark;
157:     type Error = io::Error;
158: 
159:     fn unpark(&self) -> Self::Unpark {
160:         self.park.unpark()
161:     }
162: 
163:     fn park(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
164:         self.park.park()?;
165:         self.process();
166:         Ok(())
167:     }
168: 
169:     fn park_timeout(&mut self, duration: Duration) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
170:         self.park.park_timeout(duration)?;
171:         self.process();
172:         Ok(())
173:     }
174: 
175:     fn shutdown(&mut self) {
176:         self.park.shutdown()
177:     }
178: }
